title: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances: where the real discount is

videos.script: On-demand is the price of being free to stop. If you know you will run some compute for the next year, you can sell that freedom back to AWS, for the largest discount it offers. {{freedom}} There are two instruments. Reserved Instances commit to an instance type. Savings Plans commit to dollars an hour. You will read both from the public price list, and find something surprising: they cost exactly the same. {{same}} So the choice is about what the commitment follows when the fleet changes, and the term matters far more than paying upfront. {{term}} Then the part that decides whether it saves anything. A month of the shop's instances, hour by hour, and the cost of committing to each level. Commit to the floor, and you save the most. Commit to the average, and you save less. Commit to the working-hours level, and you pay more than on demand. {{floor}} The rule is one division, and by the end you can do it in your head. {{rule}}
